result:
The root cause was `PostController.update` calling `Post.forceUpdate` with the raw, unvalidated request body — `forceUpdate` bypasses both mass-assignment protection and schema validation, so a client could write any field (`authorId`, `createdAt`, etc.) straight to the row and skip the required/length checks the create form enforces.

**Fix** (`app/Http/Controllers/PostController.ts`): `update()` now validates the body with the existing `PostPayloadSchema` (same rules as `store()`: required `title`/`excerpt`/`body`, length limits) and persists via `Post.update` instead of `Post.forceUpdate`. `Post.update` runs the model's mass-assignment filter against `Post.fillable = ['title', 'excerpt', 'body']`, so `authorId`, `createdAt`, or any other field can never be written through this endpoint, and an invalid payload now gets refused with a 422 and field errors instead of silently corrupting the post.

**Tests** (`tests/PostController.test.ts`): added a `posts.update` suite (spins up the real sqlite test DB via `migrateDatabase()` and creates real `User`/`Post` rows) covering: an attacker-supplied `authorId` is ignored and ownership stays with the original author; a `createdAt` field outside the form is not written; an empty title is rejected with 422 and leaves the post unchanged; and a non-author edit attempt still gets 403. `bun test` (6 pass) and `bun run typecheck` both pass.
